home.title: Close-to-nature forestry in practice
home.intro: A forest managed close to nature carries its own risk insurance: mixed, structured stands recover from storm, drought and bark beetle in a way that even-aged monocultures do not. This site collects the practice behind that approach — what to mark, what to leave standing, and how to let the next stand grow in under the old one.
home.principle: The guiding idea is simple: work with the stand you have. Harvest single trees rather than whole areas, keep the canopy closed, and let natural regeneration do the planting.

continuousCover.text: No clearcuts. Single-tree and group selection keeps the forest floor shaded, the microclimate stable and the soil covered at all times.

mixedStands.text: Several species per stand, chosen for the site rather than for the market. Mixture spreads risk across pests, drought years and price swings.

naturalRegeneration.text: The next generation comes from seed already on site. It costs no planting stock, roots undisturbed, and selects itself for local conditions.

home.closing: Everything here is written for people who actually walk their stands: forest owners, foresters, and anyone taking over woodland that was managed differently for the last fifty years.

gallery.title: Gallery
gallery.subtitle: What the practice looks like
gallery.intro: A few images of the kind of forest this site is about — closed canopy, several layers, plenty of structure — together with the book the approach is built on.

forestPath.alt: Forest track leading into a misty, tall mixed stand with dense green ground vegetation
forestPath.caption: An extraction track through a closed stand. Access for single-tree harvesting is planned once and used for decades, so the rest of the soil is never driven on.

oldGrowth.alt: Old, twisted trees over moss-covered boulders in dense shade
oldGrowth.caption: Deadwood, moss and old trunks: the structure nobody pays for, and the part of the stand that carries most of its species.

ravineStream.alt: Broadleaf forest on a slope with a small waterfall and stream running through it
ravineStream.caption: Ravine forest along a stream. Wet sites like this are left alone — they regenerate themselves and hold the slope together.

book.alt: Cover of the book Sylviculture d'écosystème – La sylviculture sauvage by Marie-Stella Duchiron
book.caption: Marie-Stella Duchiron, “Sylviculture d'écosystème — La sylviculture sauvage” (EDP Sciences). The reference behind most of what is described here.

gallery.note: Photographs are shown for illustration; click an image to open it at full size.

download.title: Download
download.subtitle: msgraph for Windows, Linux and QGIS
download.intro: msgraph analyses forest inventory data spatially: crown polygons, distances between neighbouring trees and histograms of stand attributes. Pick the build for your system.

windows.title: msgraph for Windows
windows.text: Standalone 64-bit executable. Download it and run it; there is nothing to install.

linux.title: msgraph for Linux
linux.text: Standalone binary for x86_64. Make it executable with chmod +x and run it from the shell.

qgisPlugin.title: msgraph QGIS plugin
qgisPlugin.text: Runs msgraph inside QGIS 3. Take the mstella_<version>.zip from the release page and install it via Plugins → Manage and Install Plugins → Install from ZIP.

s1.heading: 1. Data Protection at a Glance
s1.p1: The protection of your personal data is important to me. This Privacy Policy explains what personal data is collected when you visit this website and how such data is processed.
s1.p2: Personal data means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person.

items: IP address or anonymised IP address
technical information concerning the request and response
s3.p3: The processing of this information is necessary for the secure, reliable and efficient operation of the website. According to GitHub, the IP address of visitors to a GitHub Pages site is logged and stored for security purposes.
s3.p4: The legal basis for this processing is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. My legitimate interest is the secure and technically reliable provision of this website.
s3.p5: GitHub Pages acts as the hosting service for this website. As the website consists exclusively of static files, no server-side processing of your input takes place on my part, and I have no access to GitHub's server log files.
s3.p6: Further information about GitHub's processing of personal data can be found in the GitHub General Privacy Statement.
s3.p7: Because GitHub, Inc. is based in the United States, personal data — in particular your IP address — may be transferred to the USA and therefore to a third country. According to its own statements, GitHub, Inc. is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, for which the European Commission has issued an adequacy decision pursuant to Art. 45 GDPR. In addition, GitHub relies on the European Commission's standard contractual clauses (Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914) pursuant to Art. 46(2)(c) GDPR for transfers to third countries.

s4.p2: If you contact me using the email address or telephone number given on this website, the information you provide is processed for the purpose of dealing with and responding to your enquiry. This may include, in particular:

s4.p4: If your enquiry concerns the initiation or performance of a contractual relationship, the legal basis for processing is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR.
s4.p5: For other enquiries, the processing is based on my legitimate interest in responding to enquiries addressed to me pursuant to Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR.
s4.p6: Your data will be deleted when your enquiry has been conclusively dealt with and there is no legal obligation or other lawful reason to retain the data for a longer period.
s4.p7: Please note that email may be transmitted over the internet in unencrypted form. Please therefore do not send sensitive personal information by email unless this is necessary for your enquiry.

s8.heading: 8. Your Rights under the GDPR
s8.p1: Under the GDPR, you have various rights concerning your personal data. Subject to the applicable legal requirements, these include:

rights.term: the right to restriction of processing
the right to object to processing

s8.p2: Where processing is based on consent, you also have the right to withdraw your consent at any time with effect for the future.
s8.p3: To exercise your rights, you may contact me using the contact details provided above.

s9.heading: 9. Right to Object to Processing
s9.p1: Where personal data is processed on the basis of Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR, you have the right under Art. 21 GDPR to object at any time, on grounds relating to your particular situation, to the processing of your personal data.
s9.p2: In the event of an objection, I will no longer process the personal data concerned unless there are compelling legitimate grounds for the processing which override your interests, rights and freedoms, or the processing serves to assert, exercise or defend legal claims.

s10.heading: 10. Right to Lodge a Complaint
s10.p1: You have the right under Art. 77 GDPR to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority if you believe that the processing of your personal data infringes the GDPR.
s10.p2: You may in particular contact the supervisory authority responsible for your place of residence, place of work or the place of the alleged infringement.
